content.text: Epididymal pain & swelling thought to be secondary to retrograde infection or reflux of urine –
: relief of pain w/ scrotal elevation
: stroking of inner thigh causes elevation of ipsilateral testis
– enlarged epididymis, increased testicular blood flow
Serous fluid collection within the layers of the tunica vaginalis of the scrotum
: peritoneal/abdominal fluid enters the scrotum via a patent processus vaginalis that failed to close
: derived from fluid from the mesothelial lining of the tunica vaginalis (no connection to the peritoneum)
•often resolves within the first 12mo of life in infants
cystic testicular mass of varicose veins
: pampiniform venous plexus & internal spermatic vein
MC surgically correctable cause of male infertility
(increased left renal vein pressure transmitted to left gonadal vein)
Asymptomatic varicocele found in 10% of population
“bag of worms” feel superior to testicle
dilation worsens when pt is upright or w/ Valsalva
•sudden onset left sided in older man:
spermatic cord twists & cuts off testicular blood supply due to congenital malformation
: insufficient fixation of the lower pole of the testis to the tunica vaginalis (
), leading to increased mobility of the testicle
scrotal, inguinal, or lower abdominal pain
: no pain relief w/ scrotal elevation
: no elevation of testicle after stroking the inner thigh
: in pts w/ H&P suggestive of torsion, imaging should NOT be performed
▪︎preferred over U/S if torsion is very likely
